title: Host-agent registry is per-process while the image runs 4 uvicorn workers
current_behavior: The daemon's WebSocket is held by one uvicorn worker's in-memory registry; chat turns served by other workers find no session and fail with 'no desktop app is connected and no server-side sandbox is configured'. On Railway there is no Docker fallback, so the Engineer persona fails in proportion to the worker count.
expected_behavior: A paired desktop is reachable from every request for that user, or the gateway refuses host-agent support when AURA_WORKERS>1.
recommendation: Set AURA_WORKERS=1 on Railway and assert it at startup when the registry is enabled; then move host-agent routing to Redis pub/sub or a dedicated single process (ADR-011 names both). Record the Railway value in BACKEND_STATUS.md.

title: Server-side tool timeouts cut off the daemon's interactive approval; an approved write can land after the model was told it timed out
current_behavior: write_file/edit_file are cancelled server-side after 15 s (write_files 30 s, run_command 60 s because the Engineer ToolContext deadline is 60 s) while the daemon waits up to 5 minutes for a human. A later Approve still executes the write/command on the user's machine after the agent was told it timed out and may have retried. run_command longer than 60 s always times out despite its 605 s spec.
expected_behavior: A server-side timeout cancels the pending approval on the daemon, or the server waits as long as the daemon's approval window; the Engineer's effective run_command budget matches its documented 605 s.
recommendation: Send a cancel frame for the call id on timeout/cancellation and mark the approval cancelled on the daemon; give the Engineer context a deadline at least as long as the longest host-routed tool; add a backend test with a fake daemon that answers after the tool timeout.

title: D8 per-task worktree isolation is unreachable from the client
current_behavior: No client sets desktop_task_isolation, so every desktop task writes into the live checkout; the Agent Review panel is always empty and its empty-state copy promises behavior that cannot happen; DESKTOP_APP_STATUS.md presents D8/D9 as landed.
expected_behavior: A Desktop IDE chat turn requests isolation so writes land in .aura-workspaces/<session> and review/merge/discard has content.
recommendation: Add the field to buildChatRequestBody gated on the IDE, cover it in sse_agent_client tests, and correct the status doc until wired.

title: write_files is registered but not in the Engineer persona's grant
current_behavior: The Engineer model is never offered write_files, so the D6 atomic multi-file path and its daemon-side single-RPC approval are dead in practice; tests call the tool directly and bypass the grant.
expected_behavior: The grant matches the documented Engineer tool surface.
recommendation: Add write_files to the Engineer allowed_tools and add a kernel-level test that the Engineer declarations include it.

title: In a trusted root run_command has no path confinement and the hard denylist is a regex seatbelt; ADR-011's 'never merely confirmable' claim holds only for file RPCs
current_behavior: A trusted root lets an untainted Engineer turn run any command as the user's OS account with no prompt, including commands touching paths outside the root; the denylist is pattern-based and bypassable (rm -r -f, find -delete, python -c). CB-05's taint-to-confirm is done; the untainted-trusted case remains.
expected_behavior: Trusted mode is clearly a developer-only mode with a visible warning, or trusted commands keep argument-level containment for destructive verbs.
recommendation: Apply the untrusted tier's argument containment to a documented set of destructive verbs in trusted roots; label the trust toggle with the real consequence; amend ADR-011's containment section.

title: The desktop app's own sign-in token is a full 30-day, unscoped, non-refreshable device token
current_behavior: A desktop login yields a bearer valid for the whole API for 30 days, persisted client-side; revocation exists only via an endpoint no client calls.
expected_behavior: Desktop sessions follow the short-access/refresh model, or a much shorter TTL plus a reachable revoke.
recommendation: Issue a normal token pair from /desktop/login or shorten the TTL and wire the revoke endpoint in Settings.

title: run always executes in the first granted root; the backend never names a working directory
current_behavior: With multiple granted roots every run_command executes in root[0] under root[0]'s trust, while file RPCs resolve by path against any root; commands can run unprompted in a trusted root the user is not working in.
expected_behavior: The Engineer session is bound to one root chosen in the IDE and the backend passes it as cwd.
recommendation: Thread the active root through ToolContext.metadata and send cwd; refuse run when several roots are granted and none is named.

title: Pairing approval shows no device identity and the only approval UI is self-approval; device revoke is unreachable
current_behavior: A user who enters a code shown to them by someone else binds their account to an attacker's daemon; the host_agent-scoped token limits it to the socket, but the victim's Engineer writes and command output then route to the attacker's machine and no client screen can revoke.
expected_behavior: The approve step names the requesting machine and paired devices are listable and revocable from the app.
recommendation: Add device_name to start_pairing and echo it on approve; add a Paired devices list with GET /desktop/devices and the existing revoke.

title: macOS build is sandboxed without the network-client entitlement
current_behavior: A release build likely cannot open a socket to the backend; nothing has ever verified macOS.
expected_behavior: com.apple.security.network.client is present or macOS is declared unsupported.
recommendation: Add the entitlement or remove macOS from the supported list.

title: The Desktop IDE is gated to Windows, the one desktop platform CI does not gate
current_behavior: The IDE renders only on Windows; Linux CI compiles but never shows it; Windows CI jobs are advisory; /ide renders nothing on Linux/macOS.
expected_behavior: The gating CI job runs on the platform the feature ships on.
recommendation: Make the Windows jobs gating once green, or widen isDesktopIde to Linux and test there.

title: Nothing in this pass is proven: no green Host Daemon CI since 2026-09-11, no end-to-end report, no VPS workspace report
evidence: git ls-files docs/reports | grep -iE engineer|desktop|hostd -> desktop-ide-phase0-audit-2026-09-25.md only
current_behavior: All desktop/hostd claims rest on local runs recorded in docs; this pass could not run dart test or pytest either.
expected_behavior: Committed green Linux and Windows hostd CI runs plus the two reports the gap register names.
recommendation: Restore runners (CB-44), make hostd CI green on both OSes, record GAP-026's session, run verify-engineer-workspaces.sh on a host with the sandbox profile.

title: No restart-on-crash, no re-auth path, no bundled daemon: a 4401 or a crash needs a human
current_behavior: The daemon stops on token expiry (30 days) or revocation and never sends reauth, so the server's reauth branch is dead; the supervisor does not restart a crashed daemon; no binary is bundled.
expected_behavior: Supervised restart with backoff, an actionable re-pair prompt on 4401, an installer that ships the daemon.
recommendation: Implement restart in HostdSupervisor; surface 4401 as a pair-again state; bundle the daemon (M8.10).

title: A Google OAuth client secret sits in deploy/.env on this workstation (untracked)
current_behavior: The repo leak (CB-06) is fixed, but a real GOCSPX- secret remains on the developer host and the desktop build scripts read deploy/.env into --dart-define, so builds made there compile a secret in again. Whether it is the rotated or leaked value is UNKNOWN.
expected_behavior: No desktop build carries a client secret; the public Desktop-app client uses PKCE alone.
recommendation: Delete the key from deploy/.env, confirm the Google client type, and make the desktop build scripts refuse a non-empty secret unless explicitly overridden.

title: Engineer in production is desktop-only: the Docker fallback cannot exist on Railway and is off by default on the VPS
current_behavior: On aureon-ai.tech every write_file/run_command from a user without a paired desktop fails with a clear error while the tools stay declared to the model; with E3-01 the persona has no reliable execution path on the live target.
expected_behavior: Status docs and the persona prompt state that the Engineer needs a paired desktop on Railway.
recommendation: Document in BACKEND_STATUS.md; consider hiding the sandbox tools when neither runner can serve the caller.

title: Loopback /status is unauthenticated and lists granted roots and the backend URL
current_behavior: Any local process can read granted roots and pairing state without the control token (disclosed as a convenience boundary).
expected_behavior: Only liveness fields on the unauthenticated path.
recommendation: Return authenticated/backend_connected only; keep roots behind the token.

title: Stale documentation inside the desktop track
current_behavior: ADR-011 says the desktop exchange sends a client secret and that no approval screen exists; the hostd README says no pairing flow exists; command_policy's header says non-allowlisted commands are refused rather than queued; the Control Center promises isolated worktrees the client never requests.
recommendation: Fix each item when touching the file; see report section 7.
